This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is doing the Philippines later this hour,
the first stop of his trip to Asia.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn has more from Seoul.
President Trump will attend a special summit
of the U.S. and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations,
or ASEAN, in Manila.
On the sidelines of ASEAN, Trump will also attend
the first summit in two years of the Quad grouping,
which also includes Japan, India and Australia.
On his final stop in Shenzhen, China,
Trump is due to participate in a summit
of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Organization,
or APEC.
He'll then hold an unprecedented meeting
with Russian President Vladimir Putin
and China's leader Xi Jinping.
Trump says he wants to discuss nuclear arms control
with his counterparts.
But China, which has the smallest nuclear arsenal
of the three powers, says the summit will be
about promoting world peace and stability.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen
says he can get the support he needs to unseat
Chuck Schumer, a Senate Majority Leader.
Here's NPR's Eric McDaniel.
By some measures, Chuck Schumer is the most unpopular
politician in America.
Many voters don't like his party either.
Only some 40 percent hold a favorable view of Democrats.
But they did just give the Senate Minority Leader
and his party huge governing majorities.
And Senator Van Hollen actually tells NPR
that's part of a larger plea for something new.
People around the country are looking for change,
and my colleagues are listening to people around the country.
Public pressure could move senators into Van Hollen's column,
but picking the Senate Majority Leader
is a closed-door, closed-ballot election,
and it's not until December 1st anything could happen.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
One of the three men charged in the death
of a black woman found hanging from a tree in Jackson,
Mississippi, is due in court for a preliminary hearing today.
Ernest Lloyd Jr. is charged with murder.
Authorities say the three men staged the scene
of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune's killing after a drug dispute.
A group of V.U. countries have agreed
to start immediate talks with Rwanda
to set up a migrant hub for rejected asylum seekers,
as me Nicholson reports.
Germany, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Greece
are aiming to build detention centers
in the landlocked African country, Rwanda,
in an effort to deter migrants from coming to Europe.
Speaking in Vienna, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stoker
and his Danish counterpart, Mette Fredricksen,
said negotiations should be quick
so that the first deportations can start in 2027.
The scheme is different from the scrapped British deal
that planned to send people to Rwanda
to have their claims processed.
These centers will be for rejected asylum seekers
who cannot be sent to their home countries.
In Germany, there are objections to the plans
within Chancellor Fredricksen's coalition government
who warn of risks of arbitrary detention,
torture, and mistreatment.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The National Transportation Safety Board
says it plans to issue a preliminary report
within a month on Friday's collision
between a tanker and a smaller river cruise ship
docked in New Orleans.
The collision sent dozens of people into the water,
190 passengers and crew on the cruise ship survived.
Officials say no one suffered critical injuries
before remained hospitalized Monday.
The murder case against Lindsay Clancy
will go to trial for a second time.
A Massachusetts judge has set Clancy's retrial
on the killing of her three young children for late March.
Clancy's first trial ended with a hung jury,
her case has raised issues about maternal mental health.
The defense has argued that Clancy was suffering
from postpartum psychosis.
The next James Bond has been announced.
NPR's Jennifer Vanasko reports the role of the iconic
British spy as going to a familiar front runner.
The British actor Robert Pattinson
will be the seventh James Bond,
joining a list of stars that started with Sean Connery
and most recently included Daniel Craig.
He was widely considered to be a finalist in the casting race.
Pattinson is known for big movies.
He was Batman four years ago.
I'm vengeance.
A vampire in the Twilight saga.
This is the skin of the killer bill.
And one of Penelope's suitors in this summer's hit The Odyssey.
Somebody get these beggars out of here.
In a statement he called Bond a legendary character.
The next Bond movie will be directed by Doon's Denis Villeneuve.
Its release date has not yet been announced.
Jennifer Vanasko, NPR News.
And I'm Jyle Snyder.
This is NPR News.
